title: Volume 9 · e-Invoice (MyInvois) End to End
subtitle: Lessons 5–8: master data that passes validation, submission and status reading, the 72 hour cancellation window, consolidated and self-billed documents
outcomes: Prepare company and customer data so submission does not fail validation
Submit an invoice and interpret accepted, rejected and validated responses
Cancel or reject inside the 72 hour window and know when it is refused
Decide what to consolidate and when to self-bill

slides.title: Prepare the data MyInvois checks first
bullets: TIN, registration number, MSIC code and SST number are validated before anything else
A customer without a TIN is a general public sale, not a business invoice
Address and phone format matter, because the portal rejects malformed fields
Clean masters before the first submission, not after the first rejection

rows: Aeon Big TIN and BRN, address with postcode and state
Phone with country code, email on the customer
Portal taxpayer validation for the TIN

slides.notes: Validation failures are almost always master data, not software, and they arrive as a rejection notice that the finance team reads as a system failure. Run a pre-check across the customer list before go-live: every business customer needs a TIN, a registration number and a complete address. Half a day of cleaning saves a week of rejected submissions.

slides.title: Submit an invoice and read the response
bullets: Submission returns a submission ID, then accepted and rejected lists
Accepted means received; validated is a later state with a UUID and a QR code
A rejected document comes back with an error list, and it is not a tax invoice
Store the UUID and the long ID against the invoice, because the portal is the source of truth

rows: Accepted documents list with one entry
Validated with UUID and long ID
UUID written to the invoice record
QR code and validation link on the invoice

slides.notes: Two states matter and clients confuse them: accepted, which means the portal has the file, and validated, which means it is a legal tax invoice with a UUID. Show both on screen, because a finance team that treats accepted as final will print invoices that cannot be verified. The QR code is what the customer scans, so test it once end to end.

slides.title: Accepted versus validated, on one screen
bullets: Submission ID, accepted count and validated UUID are three different facts
A rejected document is not a tax invoice, so the sale is unsubstantiated until it is fixed
The QR code and validation link are what the customer uses to check the document
Record identifiers on the invoice so a later audit can trace the exact document
slides.notes: The distinction between accepted and validated is the single most useful thing to teach a finance team, because it decides whether they can post the invoice to the customer. Scroll the printed page and scan the QR code once in front of them; the moment it resolves to the portal, the process becomes real rather than theoretical.

slides.title: Reject or cancel inside 72 hours
bullets: Cancellation is limited to 72 hours after validation, and the limit is enforced by the portal
A cancellation needs a reason of up to 300 characters, so write it carefully
After the window, the remedy is a credit note or debit note, not a cancellation
Documents referenced by another document cannot be cancelled while that reference lives

rows: Same action on an older document
Invoice already referenced by a credit note

slides.notes: The 72 hour rule is a business deadline, so put it in the finance team's daily routine rather than a document. One person checks the e-Invoice dashboard each morning and cancels what needs cancelling; after that, the credit note route applies. Explain both error messages by name, so nobody spends an afternoon retrying a cancellation that can never succeed.

slides.title: What the portal will and will not allow
bullets: Cancellation is possible inside 72 hours with a reason, and refused after it
A document referenced by a credit note cannot be cancelled while that reference exists
The refused case must route to a credit note, not to a retry loop
Log every cancellation with the reason, because the portal keeps its own record
slides.notes: Two error names cover almost every failed cancellation, and knowing them saves a support call: OperationPeriodOver means the window has passed, ActiveReferencingDocuments means another document depends on this one. Teach the finance team to read the name and pick the remedy, because the portal will not offer an alternative.

slides.title: Consolidate small sales and self-bill correctly
bullets: Consolidation groups many small receipts into one monthly e-Invoice for the general public
It is allowed for B2C within the rules, but not for business customers who need their own document
Self-billed invoices are issued by the buyer, typically for imports or agent sales
Both need a policy decision, because they change who is responsible for the submission

rows: One monthly document for the period
Sum of the receipts in the month
Import purchase from an overseas supplier
Which customers are consolidated and why

slides.notes: Consolidation is a legitimate relief for counter sales and a serious problem if applied to business customers, because they cannot claim input tax without their own validated document. Write the policy per customer type, get it signed, and check the monthly consolidated total against the sales report before submitting. Self-billing needs the same clarity, since the buyer becomes the issuer.

slides.title: e-Invoice document types and tax codes
bullets: Document type tells the portal what the document is, and the wrong type invalidates it
Tax type codes map to sales tax, service tax, tourism and the exemption code
Classification codes describe the product and drive reporting
Every invoice line needs both a classification and a tax type, not just a rate

rows: 01 Invoice, 02 Credit Note, 03 Debit Note, 04 Refund Note
01 Sales Tax, 02 Service Tax, E Exemption
product classification from the portal list

slides.notes: This table is the reference sheet to leave with the finance team, because most rejections trace to one of these five rows. Classification codes need mapping for every item sold, which is a morning's work with the portal list open, and the unit code mapping catches people who sell in cartons but invoice in pieces.

slides.title: Status board for the finance team
bullets: Finance needs one screen that shows what is pending, rejected or cancelled
Rejected documents need an owner and a same-day fix, or the tax invoice does not exist
Weekly reconciliation of e-Invoice totals against the sales ledger catches drift early
Keep the evidence, because the portal keeps its own copy and yours must match

rows: 0 at the end of each day

slides.notes: Give the client a daily ten-minute routine: open the dashboard, fix rejections, cancel what must be cancelled, and confirm nothing is pending overnight. Then a monthly check that validated totals equal the sales ledger. That rhythm is what keeps an e-Invoice project out of trouble, because the portal does not wait and neither does the deadline.

lab.title: Lab · Prepare, submit, validate and cancel an e-Invoice
steps: Complete the company TIN, registration, MSIC and SST fields
Complete the customer TIN, registration, address and contact
Validate the customer TIN against the portal before invoicing
Submit a 2,640.00 invoice as document type 01 and record the submission UID
Confirm the validated state and store the UUID and long ID
Cancel the document with a reason and confirm the status
Attempt a cancellation past 72 hours and record the error name
Consolidate a month of counter sales and check the total against the sales report
lab.done: Done when the invoice is validated with a stored UUID, the cancellation succeeded inside the window, the expired attempt returned its named error, and the consolidated total matches the sales report.

quiz.question: What does an accepted submission mean?
quiz.why: Accepted means the portal received the submission. Validation, with a UUID, is the later state that makes it a legal tax invoice.

quiz.question: How long does the portal allow a validated document to be cancelled?
quiz.why: Cancellation is limited to 72 hours after validation, after which the remedy is a credit note or debit note.

quiz.question: Which customers should not be consolidated into a monthly e-Invoice?
options: Business customers needing their own document
quiz.why: Business customers need their own validated document to claim input tax, so consolidation is limited to B2C within the rules.

quiz.question: What does a self-billed invoice mean?
quiz.why: In self-billing the buyer issues the document, typically for imports or agent arrangements, which shifts responsibility for submission.

quiz.question: Which portal error appears when you cancel too late?
quiz.why: OperationPeriodOver indicates the 72 hour window has passed, so the correction must be a credit note rather than a cancellation.

memory.spine: Master data validates before anything is submitted, a submission returns two lists, and cancellation lives inside 72 hours only.

trap.what: A rejected document is resubmitted unchanged.
trap.why: The validator rejects it for exactly the same reason while the 72 hour clock keeps running, so the master data or tax code must be fixed first.

narration: e-Invoice is a deadline, not a feature. Everything starts with master data: company and customer TIN, registration, MSIC, address, and a validated TIN before the first submission. When you submit, you get a submission identifier and an accepted list, but accepted only means the portal has the file. Validated is the state that matters, because that is where the UUID and the QR code come from, and that is the legal tax invoice. Cancellation lives inside seventy two hours with a reason, and after that the remedy is a credit note, which the portal enforces with named errors. Consolidate only consumer sales, self-bill only where the rules allow, and give the finance team a daily dashboard routine: clear rejections, cancel what must be cancelled, and confirm nothing is left pending overnight. A monthly tie-out between validated totals and the sales ledger is the check that keeps the project out of trouble.
